title: Generation of cell-type-specific proteomes of neurodevelopment from human cerebral organoids
protocol: Transfer cerebral organoids from the 6-well plate used for culturing to a 5 mL falcon tube, separated by condition.
Use only healthy organoids for further analysis.
Ensure hESCs exhibit healthy stem cell morphology and are 70%–80% confluent before seeding.
Monitor the growth and development of cerebral organoids regularly under a light microscope after each critical step.
Remove excess medium from each tube.
Wash organoids with cold PBS (1×) three times.
Wash cerebral organoids with ice-cold PBS until no visible matrix remains, typically requiring 2-3 washes.
Remove PBS and add 1 mL TrypLE in each tube.
Place all tubes on a 360° rotating shaker for 30 min at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Using a 1,000 μL pipette tip, pipette up and down vigorously to break the cerebral organoid into cell clumps and individual cells.
Incubate for an additional 15 minutes.
Add 2 mL of FACS buffer containing PBS/FBS 98/2 (v/v) to stop the enzymatic reaction and pipette up and down to break down clumps with a 1,000 μL pipette tip.
Spin down tubes for 5 min at 200 × g at room temperature (20°C–23°C).
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Pass the resuspended cells through a 37 μm strainer to remove remaining aggregates and non-dissociated tissue.
Perform a viable cell count using trypan blue.
Set compensation parameters for multicolor FACS.
Determine appropriate gates based on fluorescent reporters to isolate cerebral organoid-derived cells by cell type.
Use unstained organoids as a negative control to determine optimal settings for gating and discerning positive from negative cells.
Add a viability dye (such as DAPI, 1:100) in all samples, including the controls, to separate live from dead cells during cell sorting.
Sort enriched (i.e., YFP+) and depleted (i.e., YFP-) populations using the optimized parameters.
Follow manufacturer instructions for use of cell sorters.
Ensure sorting efficiency is at least 90%.
Collect sorted cells in 15 mL falcon tubes.
Wash samples.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 3 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant without disturbing the pellet and wash with cold PBS.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 3 min at 4°C (optional to spin supernatant as well).
Transfer samples to Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant.
Add around 200 μL of UREA lysis buffer.
Incubate for 30 min in ice.
Snap freeze samples in liquid nitrogen.
Defrost the samples on ice.
Sonicate the samples using a water bath sonicator at 4°C, alternating 30 seconds on and 30 seconds off for 30 minutes total.
Centrifuge the samples at 12,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a clean Eppendorf tube.
Quantitate the total protein in each sample using a BCA assay as per manufacturer instructions.
Top up sample volumes to 100 μL with 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Add 10 μL of 60 mM DTT in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate for protein denaturation, achieving a final concentration of 6 mM.
Incubate the samples on a thermoblock at 1200 × g for 45 min at 45°C.
Add 11 μL of 100 mM iodoacetamide in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate for protein alkylation, achieving a final concentration of 18 mM.
Incubate the samples on a thermoblock at 1200 × g for 45 min at room temperature in the dark.
Trypsinize all samples by adding Trypsin/Lys-C Mix (at a 1:25 protein ratio).
Incubate the samples overnight on a thermoblock at 1200 × g at room temperature.
Dilute the samples with 13.8 μL of 10% trifluoroacetic acid in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, achieving a final concentration of 1% (v/v).
Incubate the samples on a thermoblock at 1200 × g for 20 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge the samples at 13,000 × g for 10 min and transfer the supernatant to a clean Eppendorf tube.
Use Pierce C18 zip tip pipette tips as per manufacturer instructions to remove salts, lipids, DNA, and other contaminants from the samples.
Elute bound peptides with 3 μL of ACN/H2O 65/35 (v/v) + 0.1% TFA.
Dilute eluted peptide samples in 42 μL with H2O + 0.1% TFA.
Centrifuge the diluted samples at 3,500 × g for 10 min prior to analysis.
Inject 40 μL of sample onto the LC-MS/MS system for analysis using a Thermo Fisher nano liquid chromatography setup coupled with Q Exactive HFX mass spectrometer.
